disclaimer: Fictional synthetic exemplars for drafting practice only. No real student data. Not legal advice.

exemplars.title: Grade 3 — SLD, basic reading/decoding (dyslexia profile)
exemplars.profile_summary: A third-grade student with average oral language and strong hands-on reasoning who reads single words with common vowel patterns (vowel teams, r-controlled, CVCe) at 42% accuracy and reads connected text at 28 WCPM. Spelling is phonetic and inconsistent. The student avoids reading aloud and sometimes tears up during timed reading tasks.
strengths: Strong verbal storytelling and vocabulary when listening
Good classroom citizenship and peer relationships
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports nightly reading is a struggle and is worried the student will fall behind; asks for daily practice ideas that do not turn into conflict.
evaluation_data: Standardized achievement: word reading and spelling standard scores in the low-average to below-average range; listening comprehension average
Decoding inventory: 42% accuracy on vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, and CVCe words
Word reading fluency: 28 WCPM on grade-3 probes (fall benchmark 70+)
Evaluation team documented a pattern consistent with dyslexia; parent history of reading difficulty

plaafp.academic: The student decodes grade-3 single words with common vowel patterns at 42% accuracy and reads grade-3 passages at 28 WCPM with 86% accuracy. Listening comprehension is a relative strength. Written spelling shows letter-sound approximations but omits vowel teams and common spelling patterns.
plaafp.functional: The student avoids oral reading, requests to leave for water during reading block, and shows frustration (pushing materials away) during timed probes; frustration is reduced with chunked, untimed practice and choice of text.
plaafp.impact: Basic reading and spelling deficits related to the specific learning disability (dyslexia) prevent access to grade-level text across all content areas and limit independent written work, requiring specially designed reading instruction and text access supports.

baselines.skill: Decoding vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, CVCe

goals.condition: Given grade-3 word lists and decodable passages targeting vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, and CVCe patterns
goals.skill: read targeted patterns accurately and apply them to connected text
goals.measurement: Weekly curriculum-based decoding inventory; teacher running records
goals.schedule: weekly probes; goal reviewed each quarter

goals.condition: Given a mastered grade-3 passage and repeated reading practice
goals.skill: read aloud with accuracy and appropriate rate
goals.target: 65 WCPM with 95% accuracy across 2 consecutive passages
goals.measurement: Grade-3 CBM oral reading fluency probes

goals.condition: Given a dictated list of 10 words containing taught patterns
goals.skill: spell words using taught vowel patterns
goals.measurement: Weekly dictation; analysis of error patterns

exemplars.progress_reporting: Progress reports with current data every 9 weeks, concurrent with report cards; parent may request additional updates.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Mild frustration/frustration-avoidance behavior responds to chunking, untimed practice, and choice; if avoidance escalates, the team will conduct an FBA and add a behavior support plan.
supplementary_aids_services: Access to audiobooks and text-to-speech for grade-level content
Pre-teaching of reading passages and vocabulary before whole-class reading
Partner reading with a fluent peer for content-area text
Visual anchor charts for vowel patterns in the classroom
accommodations: Extended time on reading and writing tasks
Read-aloud of directions and test items when decoding is not the target skill
Chunked assignments with checkpoints
Oral responses in place of written where decoding/writing is not assessed
Reduced copying from the board; provide printed notes
program_modifications: None — the student accesses grade-level standards with accommodations and SDI.
personnel_supports: Quarterly progress-monitoring data review with the reading interventionist
Access to the district dyslexia intervention materials and training
exemplars.lre_statement: The student participates in the general education classroom for the full day except during scheduled SDI. Pull-out reading instruction is necessary because intensive, sequential decoding instruction requires a quiet, small-group setting that cannot be delivered without disrupting the general classroom; the student returns to general education for all content instruction with supports.
exemplars.placement: General education classroom with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21% of the day). Placement determined after goals/services, starting from general education.
exemplars.assessment: Participates in AASA and district assessments with accommodations (extended time, read-aloud of directions, chunking). MOWR third-grade reading requirements considered; no alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student has shown a pattern of summer regression in decoding fluency during past breaks and would lose access to critical early reading instruction; ESY reading services proposed for 3x/week for 60 minutes over a 5-week session, to be confirmed with spring data. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
source_lineage: Missouri DESE PLAAFP and SMART Goal rubrics
exemplars.notes: Dyslexia diagnosis must be documented per A.R.S. §15-763. Baseline data fields align to the tool's goal checker.

exemplars.title: Grade 4 — SLD, reading fluency
exemplars.profile_summary: A fourth-grade student who decodes accurately but reads slowly and word-by-word, which limits comprehension of grade-level text. Oral reading is 62 WCPM with 94% accuracy; comprehension of grade-4 text is 60%.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent says the student understands ideas when read aloud but cannot finish reading assignments in time.
evaluation_data: Oral reading fluency: 62 WCPM (grade-4 fall benchmark 90–110)
Accuracy: 94% on grade-4 passages
Reading comprehension: 60% on grade-4 curriculum-based questions
Processing speed below average on cognitive measures; decoding skills in the average range

plaafp.academic: The student reads grade-4 text accurately (94%) but at 62 WCPM, which is below the fall benchmark, causing incomplete reading of content-area assignments and reduced comprehension (60% on literal and inferential questions). Listening comprehension is age-appropriate.
plaafp.functional: Work completion drops when tasks require extended silent reading; the student rushes and skips words, then reports not understanding the text.
plaafp.impact: Fluency deficits related to the specific learning disability slow access to grade-level text and reduce comprehension, requiring fluency instruction and access supports in content classes.

goals.condition: Given grade-4 passages with repeated reading and phrase-cued practice
goals.skill: read aloud with appropriate rate and phrasing
goals.target: 100 WCPM with 96% accuracy across 2 consecutive probes
goals.measurement: Weekly grade-4 CBM oral reading fluency probes; prosody rubric

goals.condition: Given grade-4 informational text read with a fluency support and a graphic organizer
goals.skill: answer literal and inferential questions and summarize main idea

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with report cards, with graphs of fluency probes and comprehension checks.

services.type: Special education — reading fluency and comprehension (SDI)
Supplementary — fluency practice in general classroom
services.provider: General education teacher with SPED consultation

supplementary_aids_services: Audiobooks and text-to-speech for content-area reading
Shortened reading passages with equivalent content objectives
accommodations: Extended time on reading assignments and tests
Read-aloud of directions and non-reading test items
Frequent check-ins to monitor understanding
Option to respond orally to demonstrate comprehension
personnel_supports: Monthly consultation between SPED and general education teachers on fluency routines
Training on repeated-reading and phrase-cued text strategies
exemplars.lre_statement: The student is included in general education all day except for four 40-minute SDI sessions. Pull-out is required for repeated-reading and decoding-practice routines that need a quiet small-group setting. The student returns for all core instruction with text-access supports.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA reading and all district assessments with extended time and read-aloud of non-reading items. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. No documented regression/recoupment data support ESY at this time; parents will be given fluency practice materials. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Shows a fluency-only SLD profile where dyslexia is not documented; the tool should still prompt for the SLD/dyslexia statement.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — SLD, reading comprehension
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student who reads grade-level text fluently (108 WCPM, 97% accuracy) but struggles to identify main ideas, make inferences, and summarize, scoring 45% on comprehension checks.
strengths: Strong memory for facts and details
Kind and cooperative in group work
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent notices the student can read anything but cannot explain what was read.
evaluation_data: Oral reading fluency: 108 WCPM / 97% accuracy (grade-5 benchmark met)
Comprehension: 45% on literal/inferential questions; 1/5 correct on summarization rubric
Vocabulary: grade-level on direct assessment
Pattern of comprehension difficulty with intact decoding identified by the evaluation team

plaafp.academic: The student decodes and reads fluently but earns 45% on grade-5 comprehension checks and 1/5 on summarization, especially for inferential questions and main-idea identification. Vocabulary is a relative strength.
plaafp.functional: The student can recount isolated details but not organize or explain them, and becomes discouraged during discussion-based tasks that require synthesis.
plaafp.impact: Comprehension deficits related to the specific learning disability reduce performance across reading, science, and social studies, requiring explicit strategy instruction and scaffolded text tasks.

goals.area: Reading comprehension — inference and main idea
goals.condition: Given a grade-5 informational text and a graphic organizer
goals.skill: identify main idea and supporting details and answer inferential questions with text evidence
goals.target: 80% accuracy across 3 of 4 consecutive weekly checks
goals.measurement: Curriculum-based comprehension checks scored with answer key/rubric

goals.condition: Given a grade-5 narrative or informational passage and a summary frame
goals.skill: write a 3–5 sentence summary including main idea and key details
goals.measurement: District summary rubric (main idea, details, organization, conventions)

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks; teacher attaches comprehension check samples and summary rubric scores.

services.type: Special education — written language for summaries (SDI)

supplementary_aids_services: Graphic organizers for all reading tasks
Text outlines/highlighted main ideas for content-area reading
accommodations: Extended time on reading tasks
Option to answer comprehension questions orally
Chunked text sections with check-ins
Use of a checklist for main-idea and inference steps
personnel_supports: Training on explicit comprehension strategy instruction (e.g., reciprocal teaching)
Monthly coordination with the grade-5 team on text modifications
exemplars.lre_statement: The student participates in general education for all content except SDI sessions. Pull-out provides explicit strategy instruction in a small group that cannot be delivered effectively during whole-class reading; the student applies strategies in general education with organizers and accommodations.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA with extended time and oral-response option on reading comprehension items (as allowed); MOWR requirements considered for grade-level reading expectations. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. A pattern of summer regression in comprehension strategy use was noted by the prior-year teacher; ESY for reading comprehension 2x/week for 45 minutes is recommended pending spring progress data. Decision by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Illustrates comprehension-only SLD with fluent decoding — useful for the tool's 'profile builder' branching.

exemplars.title: Grade 2 — SLD, math calculation
exemplars.profile_summary: A second-grade student with strong oral language and reading skills who struggles with addition and subtraction within 100 and lacks automaticity with basic facts, scoring 30% on place-value/regrouping tasks and 8 correct digits per minute on fact fluency.
strengths: Strong verbal reasoning and reading comprehension
Engaged in math games and manipulatives
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is concerned about nightly math homework conflicts and finger counting for basic facts.
evaluation_data: Calculation: 30% accuracy on two-digit addition/subtraction with regrouping
Math fact fluency: 8 correct digits per minute
Math reasoning/problem solving: average
Comprehensive evaluation ruled out lack of instruction and confirmed a specific learning disability in math calculation

plaafp.academic: The student computes two-digit problems with regrouping at 30% accuracy and completes 8 correct digits per minute on fact fluency (target ~20+). Math reasoning is age-appropriate, and the student can verbally explain strategies but loses track of sequence and place value in written work.
plaafp.functional: Math homework takes 45+ minutes and often ends in frustration; the student uses fingers for simple facts and avoids independent practice.
plaafp.impact: Calculation and fluency deficits related to the specific learning disability interfere with grade-2 math standards and with completing multi-step tasks, requiring explicit computation instruction and fluency practice.

goals.condition: Given 10 two-digit addition/subtraction problems with regrouping and place-value supports
goals.skill: compute accurately using a taught sequence

goals.condition: Given a 1-minute mixed addition/subtraction fact probe within 20
goals.target: 20 correct digits/min with 95% accuracy across 3 probes

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with report cards; facts graph shared at conferences.

services.type: Supplementary — guided practice in general classroom
services.provider: General education teacher with SPED consultation

supplementary_aids_services: Place-value charts and multiplication/addition fact cards
accommodations: Extended time on math tasks
Reduced number of practice items while preserving skill coverage
Use of manipulatives and reference charts during classroom work (not on assessments where prohibited)
Oral explanation of the process to demonstrate understanding
personnel_supports: Consultation on CRA sequence and fluency routines
exemplars.lre_statement: The student receives math SDI in a small group because explicit remediation with manipulatives and fluency practice requires immediate corrective feedback and pacing not possible in a whole-class lesson. The student participates in general education math for concept development and all other subjects.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: District math assessments with extended time and manipulatives per assessment policy; AASA as scheduled. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Math fact fluency showed substantial regression over summer break with slow recoupment in the prior year; ESY math for 2x/week, 30 minutes, 5 weeks is proposed based on that retroactive data. Decision by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Good exemplar for the ESY regression/recoupment documentation path.

exemplars.title: Grade 4 — SLD, math problem solving/reasoning
exemplars.profile_summary: A fourth-grade student with accurate computation skills who cannot choose operations or set up multi-step word problems, scoring 2/10 on grade-4 problem-solving tasks despite strong fact fluency.
strengths: Fluent with basic facts and computation
Persistent and calm during structured tasks
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent reports the student can 'do the math' but freezes on word problems and standardized test questions.
evaluation_data: Computation: 92% accuracy on grade-4 whole-number operations
Problem solving: 2/10 multi-step word problems correct
Math vocabulary: below average on curriculum vocabulary check
Evaluation team identified a specific learning disability in math problem solving

plaafp.academic: The student computes grade-4 operations accurately (92%) but solves only 2/10 multi-step word problems, often choosing the wrong operation or missing relevant information. Math vocabulary and representation (drawing the problem) are areas of need.
plaafp.functional: The student avoids word problems, guesses operations to finish quickly, and needs prompts to slow down and use a strategy.
plaafp.impact: Problem-solving deficits related to the specific learning disability affect access to grade-4 math standards and state assessment performance, requiring strategy instruction and scaffolded problem-solving routines.

goals.condition: Given grade-4 multi-step word problems and a problem-solving checklist (understand, plan, solve, check)
goals.skill: identify relevant information, select operations, and solve accurately
goals.measurement: Weekly problem-solving probes scored with rubric

goals.condition: Given instruction on grade-4 math academic vocabulary
goals.skill: use and explain terms accurately in problem contexts

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with scored problem-solving probes and vocabulary data.
supplementary_aids_services: Highlighted key numbers/vocabulary in word problems
Pre-teaching of math vocabulary before units
accommodations: Extended time on word-problem tasks and assessments
Read-aloud of word problems when decoding is not the target
Chunked problems (one step at a time)
Use of reference sheet for vocabulary/steps
personnel_supports: Co-planning time with the grade-4 math teacher
Training on schema-based instruction and bar modeling
exemplars.lre_statement: Pull-out SDI provides explicit strategy instruction and guided practice with immediate feedback that cannot be provided in a whole-class pacing; the student participates in all general education math lessons and applies strategies with scaffolds.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: AASA math with extended time, read-aloud of non-math-reasoning items where permitted, and chunking. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. No significant regression in problem-solving strategies was documented; parent will receive practice activities. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Shows the difference between calculation and problem-solving SLD goals.

exemplars.title: Grade 3 — SLD, written expression
exemplars.profile_summary: A third-grade student with strong oral language and story ideas who writes short, incomplete sentences with frequent capitalization, punctuation, and spelling errors; 35% of sentences are complete, and paragraphs lack a topic sentence.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent says the student's writing does not match the stories the student tells at home.
evaluation_data: Written expression: 35% complete sentences on a 20-sentence writing sample
Paragraph writing: 1/4 on topic-sentence rubric
Oral language: average to above-average for language structure and vocabulary
Evaluation team identified a specific learning disability in written expression

plaafp.academic: The student writes 35% complete sentences, omits capitals/end punctuation in 6 of 10 sentences, and produces paragraphs without a clear topic sentence (1/4 on rubric). Oral expression is stronger than written expression.
plaafp.functional: The student rushes written work, erases frequently, and often says they 'don't know what to write' without a graphic organizer.
plaafp.impact: Written-expression deficits related to the specific learning disability limit performance on grade-3 writing standards and across content areas requiring written responses, requiring explicit instruction and scaffolded writing tasks.

goals.condition: Given a sentence-writing task and an editing checklist
goals.skill: write complete sentences with correct capitalization and end punctuation
goals.target: 85% complete sentences with correct conventions across 3 consecutive writing samples
goals.measurement: Weekly writing samples scored with a conventions checklist

goals.condition: Given a graphic organizer and a topic
goals.skill: write a 4–5 sentence paragraph with a topic sentence and supporting details
goals.measurement: District paragraph rubric (topic sentence, details, organization, conventions)

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with writing samples and rubric scores.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: Writing avoidance (putting head down, claiming inability) responds to graphic organizers, oral rehearsal, and chunked tasks; no FBA needed at this time.

services.type: Supplementary — writing supports in general education
services.provider: General education teacher with SPED consultation

supplementary_aids_services: Word banks and personal spelling dictionaries
accommodations: Extended time on writing tasks
Scribing or speech-to-text for content-area writing when conventions are not the target
Reduced copying; provided notes
Chunked writing assignments with checkpoints
exemplars.lre_statement: Pull-out SDI provides explicit sentence and paragraph instruction with immediate feedback; the student writes in general education with organizers and accommodations and participates in all other subjects fully.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: District writing assessments with extended time and use of a graphic organizer; AASA as scheduled with writing accommodations per policy. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. Writing conventions showed regression over summer and slow recoupment in the prior year; ESY writing 2x/week for 45 minutes is proposed based on that data. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Third example of a writing profile; useful for snippet variants around sentence vs. paragraph goals.

exemplars.title: Grade 5 — SLD, mixed reading and written language
exemplars.profile_summary: A fifth-grade student with dual eligibility (SLD and SLI) who reads multisyllabic words at 55% accuracy and writes disorganized multi-paragraph responses; oral language shows word-finding difficulties.
strengths: Creative ideas and strong engagement in discussion
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent is concerned about the student's confidence and the amount of time homework takes.
evaluation_data: Multisyllabic decoding: 55% accuracy
Reading comprehension: 65% on grade-5 checks
Written expression: 1.5/4 on district rubric
Speech-language evaluation documented word-finding and syntax needs; dual eligibility determined

plaafp.academic: The student decodes multisyllabic words at 55% accuracy, comprehends grade-5 text at 65%, and scores 1.5/4 on the district written-expression rubric. Word-finding pauses and syntax errors affect oral and written responses.
plaafp.functional: The student takes longer to formulate answers, loses ideas mid-sentence, and avoids sharing written work; benefits from wait time, sentence starters, and graphic organizers.
plaafp.impact: Mixed reading/writing and language deficits related to the disabilities reduce access to grade-level literacy tasks and require integrated SDI and speech-language services.

goals.condition: Given grade-5 multisyllabic words and syllable-division strategies
goals.skill: decode using syllable patterns and morphology

goals.condition: Given a planning organizer and word bank
goals.skill: write an organized multi-paragraph response with accurate sentence structure

goals.condition: Given structured speaking tasks and sentence frames
goals.skill: use target vocabulary and complete sentences with correct grammar
goals.measurement: Language sample analysis; curriculum-based oral tasks

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with reading probes, writing rubric scores, and SLP data.
supplementary_aids_services: Wait time and rehearsal before oral responses
accommodations: Extended time on reading and writing tasks
Speech-to-text for long writing assignments when spelling/conventions are not the target
Oral responses when feasible
Chunked assignments with checkpoints
personnel_supports: Joint planning time for SPED/SLP strategies
General education teacher training on wait time and scaffolded language supports
exemplars.lre_statement: The student receives pull-out SDI and speech-language therapy in small settings because intensive decoding and language intervention require focused practice and immediate feedback. The student is included for all content instruction with integrated language and literacy supports; some SLP sessions are push-in to support carryover.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource and speech services (outside regular class less than 21% when combined).
exemplars.assessment: AASA and district assessments with extended time, chunking, and permitted language supports. Alternate assessment criteria not met.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. The student showed substantial regression/recoupment concerns in decoding and language after the prior summer; ESY combined reading/language sessions 3x/week for 45 minutes are proposed. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Demonstrates dual eligibility and integrated services; useful for the tool's service-grid validation.

exemplars.title: Grade 2 — SLD, oral language/listening comprehension
exemplars.profile_summary: A second-grade student who follows single-step directions but struggles with multi-step directions and retelling stories, scoring 40% on listening tasks and 2/5 on story retell.
exemplars.parent_concerns: Parent notices the student does not remember directions at home and asks for repetition constantly.
evaluation_data: Listening comprehension: 40% on grade-2 tasks
Multi-step directions: follows 1/5 three-step directions
Story retell: 2/5 story elements
SLD eligibility determined in the area of oral expression/listening comprehension

plaafp.academic: The student follows one-step directions but completes only 1/5 three-step directions and includes 2/5 story elements in retell. Decoding is on grade level; listening comprehension is the primary weakness.
plaafp.functional: The student relies on peers to clarify directions, needs frequent repetition, and can appear off-task during oral instruction.
plaafp.impact: Listening-comprehension and oral-language deficits related to the specific learning disability affect access to oral instruction across all subjects, requiring repetition, visual supports, and explicit listening-strategy instruction.

goals.condition: Given oral two- and three-step directions with visual cues
goals.schedule: daily data; weekly review; quarterly reporting

goals.condition: Given a grade-2 story read aloud and a retell graphic organizer
goals.skill: retell with characters, setting, problem, events, and solution

exemplars.progress_reporting: Every 9 weeks with listening-task data and retell rubrics.
exemplars.special_factor_behavior: The student may appear inattentive due to listening demands; visual supports and repetition are used. No behavioral concern requiring an FBA at this time.

services.type: Supplementary — listening supports in general education
services.provider: General education teacher with SPED consultation

supplementary_aids_services: Visual schedules and picture cues for directions
accommodations: Simplified/repeated directions
Visual supports on tasks
Extended time to process and respond
Check for understanding after directions
exemplars.lre_statement: Pull-out SDI provides focused listening and retell practice in a quiet setting; the student is fully included otherwise with visual and repetition supports so access to oral instruction is maintained.
exemplars.placement: General education with pull-out resource services (outside regular class less than 21%).
exemplars.assessment: District assessments with directions read aloud, repeated, and visually supported; AASA as scheduled. No alternate assessment.
exemplars.esy: Team considered ESY. No documented regression in listening skills; parents will receive summer language activities. Decision documented by the 45-day deadline.
exemplars.notes: Useful contrast with SLI eligibility; the tool should ask whether the need is better served under SLD or SLI.
